One Pennsylvania sale, traced

A public-data demonstration of controlled sale entry. Each figure was read from public documents, checked by code against the line it came from, approved, and written into an Excel comparison grid without touching a formula. Select a figure to see where it came from.

    What ran, in order

    One recorded run against a real PostgreSQL database, with an application role for each job: reading, reviewing, writing. The model was called once; the run replays its recorded answer.

      The workbook, before and after

      Files

        Not shown here

        • Local-source demonstration; Microsoft tenant integration not demonstrated. The documents were read from a local folder.
        • Excel for Mac, not desktop Excel on a Windows 365 runner. The copy on this machine is not activated, so it recalculated the file and could not save it; the delivered file is the written file, with the same hash as the one Excel recalculated.
        • No party to the sale was contacted. The deed image was not retrieved; the instrument number comes from the county assessment record.
        • The grid is ours, built to stand in for a firm's model. Its adjustment convention is one of several in use.
        • Word reports, a review queue and multi-agent quality control are left out.

        Next step: establish whether this controlled entry pattern fits your workbook, and define the template-mapping and acceptance work for discovery.
